No, that is not true. In Switzerland, **obligatory basic health insurance (LaMal/KVG)** must be taken out **within three months of establishing residence** (i.e., moving to Switzerland or registering with the municipality). There is no legal option to sign up later without risking disadvantages.

If you fail to obtain this insurance within the three-month window, you may face **penalties**, **additional administrative costs**, and **legal consequences**. Furthermore, without valid health insurance, you cannot access medical services covered by the basic insurance scheme.

Switzerland has a **compulsory health insurance system**—every resident is legally required to have it. There are no exceptions to the three-month rule for taking out the mandatory basic insurance.

If you are moving to Switzerland, you should secure this insurance as soon as you establish residence to avoid complications.
